title: Client partial-checksum idempotency windows for dedup-safe billing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: We observe transient duplicate billing in edge cases where clients retry after partial failures (network timeouts, client crashes) and the server processes partially identical payloads that differ only in non-deterministic metadata (timestamps, ephemeral request IDs). Existing safeguard mechanisms (global nonces and request seals) reduce duplicates but do not cover: 1) resource-constrained clients that cannot maintain long-lived nonces, 2) cases where clients re-send a request after failover with slightly altered fields, and 3) backfilled/queued delivery patterns where identical user intent is split across several sub-requests. This ticket proposes a server-side idempotency layer that leverages a client-provided partial checksum (sha256 over canonicalized important fields) combined with an adaptive idempotency window. The goal is to prevent duplicate consumption charges while preserving low-latency admission and compatibility with current SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts optional header X-Partial-Checksum (base64 sha256) and records a short-lived fingerprint in a dedupe store
If an arriving request carries a matching checksum and occurs within the adaptive idempotency window, the server returns the original response (200/201) without double-charging usage metrics
Idempotency window is dynamically chosen based on client behavior class (SDK, non-SDK, queued), defaulting to 30s for interactive and up to 24h for bulk-backfill with explicit flag
Rate limiting interacts with idempotency: duplicate requests within window do not increment quota counters or meter tokens twice
No added false-positive dedup rate above 0.01% for production traffic (measured in canary)
All changes have unit and integration tests; QA verifies billing invariants under retry storms and simulated partial failure patterns
Design review and security review completed and signed off before prod rollout
technical_design: Overview: Introduce a lightweight dedupe index (D-index) keyed by <customer_id, model_id, partial_checksum, entropy_salt_bucket>. The partial checksum is computed by clients by canonicalizing the request payload (text/prompts, truncated metadata fields) and hashing. Server-side, we compute a canonicalized server-side fingerprint to validate and normalize client checksum where possible. D-index entries are written atomically alongside a provisional usage ledger entry but marked as 'dedupe-guard' so that only the first writer commits final billing. Implementation details: 1) Storage: use a time-partitioned Redis cluster for low-latency lookups with TTL per entry driven by the adaptive window. For long windows (bulk), fall back to a sharded Cassandra table for persistence and reconciliation sweep. 2) Entropy salt buckets: to reduce accidental collision impact, the server assigns an entropy_bucket based on a small per-request server nonce and stores bucket id in D-index. This prevents an attacker from constructing collisions across many customers. 3) Atomicity: use a compare-and-set pattern with Lua scripts in Redis to atomically create D-index entries and attach a provisional ledger id. If CAS fails, fetch the existing ledger id and replay stored response. 4) Billing interaction: consumption-metrics ingestion pipeline checks the D-index marker. If a request is marked as duplicate, the metrics pipeline emits a dedupe_inspected metric and suppresses token accounting for charges. 5) Backwards-compatibility: SDKs will add optional checksum header; servers accept missing header and fall back to existing nonce/ack protocols. 6) Security: partial checksum design intentionally excludes sensitive user data by instructing SDKs to exclude PII fields. 7) Admin controls: per-tenant toggles (off/on/observe-only) + per-tenant max idempotency window setting. 8) Monitoring & Auditing: store dedupe decisions with trace-id for full auditability. Implementation plan broken into small PRs: checksum validation + SDK opt-in -> server D-index lookup -> atomic write + provisional ledger -> metrics suppression + reconciliation sweep.
rollout_plan: Week 1: SDK opt-in release (python/js): add X-Partial-Checksum header and canonicalization helper (observe-only mode). Deploy to 10% of SDK user traffic
Week 2: Server-side D-index read-only collect mode (record checksums, no suppression) across canary clusters
Week 3: Canary write mode with default short idempotency window (30s) and CAS writes in staging. Run synthetic retry storm tests and billing smoke tests
Week 4: Gradually enable suppression for low-risk tenants (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and increase windows for configured bulk customers
Post-rollout: Run a 48h reconciliation sweep for long-window dedupe entries stored in Cassandra to ensure no missed charges; iterate on false-positive threshold
monitoring_and_metrics: alerts: dedupe.duplicate_rate > 0.5% for top-10 revenue customers
trace-links for each dedupe decision emitted to logging/observability
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: checksum collisions leading to undercharging. Mitigation: entropy_salt_bucket + low default windows + collision sampling to detect anomalies
Risk: added latency on hot request path. Mitigation: use fast Redis lookups, move heavy reconciliation to async background jobs, optimize Lua scripts, measure p95 impact in canary

Risk: clients compute checksum incorrectly leading to missed dedupe. Mitigation: provide canonicalization helpers in SDKs, fall back to server-side canonicalization heuristics, observe-only telemetry to validate correctness before enforcement
Risk: state explosion in Redis for long windows. Mitigation: TTL enforcement, fall back to Cassandra for long-lived entries, per-tenant caps, and auto-expiry sweeps
notes: We intentionally keep the checksum partial (selected fields) to balance privacy and dedupe effectiveness. This mechanism complements existing nonce/lease systems rather than replacing them. For highest-assurance enterprise customers we recommend a combined approach: client-signed usage certificates + the partial-checksum dedupe index.
